children: According to Sina Finance, sources said the main reason NVIDIA's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation was its view that he had not been candid and had lied. The allegations emerged amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Huang acknowledged an affair on November 8, and further rumors surfaced in the following days, including one allegedly involving a direct subordinate. A person familiar with the board's discussions told Wired that Huang's alleged lying dated from October 2025 through the recent events.

Sources said the board was furious after the first affair became public. One person familiar with the board's thinking said the primary reason for Huang's departure was lying, adding that the issue concerned integrity and trust. Board members, including Chairman Harvey Jones, have recently sought to quell discussion of Huang returning, saying his conduct violated NVIDIA's policies and corporate governance rules. Jones did not respond to a request for comment. NVIDIA spokesperson John Rizzo declined to comment. John Fisher, a vice president at Trident, the public relations firm representing Huang, said Huang had voluntarily resigned from NVIDIA and declined further comment.

At an all-hands meeting on November 18, Jones said accepting Huang's resignation was not an easy decision, but that Huang's disclosed personal conduct and lack of candor violated the company's code of conduct, standards, and values. Thousands of NVIDIA employees and Elon Musk have called for Huang to return. Huang said he would be honored to serve again as CEO. On Friday, U.S. President Donald Trump said he hoped Huang would get another chance and told reporters that Huang had made some wrong decisions but was very smart; Trump said he hoped Huang would apologize sincerely. Reports said a minority of board members also favored Huang's return, while Jones did not respond to questions about reported divisions on the board.

Some employees objected to the board's quick acceptance of Huang's resignation, saying they believed he had been forced out. Interim CEO Colette Kress said employees were most concerned about NVIDIA's falling share price, followed by the board's decision on Huang. She responded to the first concern with accelerated pay raises but did not promise to disclose the board's investigation findings or internal discussions. One computer scientist said the company had no plan to explain transparently what happened, describing the matter as a black box.

title: NVIDIA Board's Main Reason for Ousting Jensen Huang: Lack of Candor
